title: Search record, version 2
description: Immutable record of one owned branch-and-bound search under SPEC-0003, sufficient to repeat it. A search outcome is the executive's own claim that it exhausted its node tree; it is distinct from one relaxation's termination and is never an exact-arithmetic certificate. Version 2 carries the caller's extension policy and one summary per permitted extension under SPEC-0004. Absent measurements are omitted rather than serialized as null.

backend.description: Identifier recorded for the relaxation service.

backend_version.description: Version reported by the relaxation backend itself, not assumed by the executive.

outcome.description: Engine-owned search outcome. Only proven_optimal, proven_infeasible and unbounded_or_infeasible are completed proofs; a limit, interruption or failure never implies one.

objective.description: Independently recomputed original objective of the incumbent, never a backend-reported value. Finite when present.

dual_bound.description: Best valid dual bound over open nodes, present only when a relaxation proved one.

gap.description: Relative gap between incumbent and dual bound, present only when finite.

candidate.description: Accepted incumbent in original variable IDs.

validation.description: Independent original-model validation of the incumbent, as defined by SPEC-0001. Unbounded sides and continuous domain checks are explicitly null there.

nodes_pruned_infeasible.description: Nodes closed by a proven infeasible relaxation or an empty branch domain.

nodes_pruned_bound.description: Nodes closed by a valid dual bound against the incumbent.

open_nodes_remaining.description: Nodes still open when the search stopped.

relaxations_solved.description: Relaxation solves dispatched to the backend.

forfeited.description: Whether any node permanently lost the search's proof claim. Recorded explicitly so a reader can see why a completed-looking search claimed nothing.

warnings.description: Executive warnings, retained even on success.

extensions.description: What each permitted extension did, in extension-identity order. Empty when no extension was permitted, so a record cannot conceal that extensions influenced it.

authority.description: Acceptance boundary the core applied, derived from the category and never chosen by the extension. Absent for a refused category.

failures.description: Bounded distinct failures. Counters stay exact while retained messages are capped, so an extension refused once per node cannot grow a record with the search.

elapsed_ms.description: Measured elapsed wall-clock time in milliseconds. Deliberately excluded from reproducibility comparison: it measures the host, not the search.
